problem.statement: Given nums and target, return indices of two numbers whose sum is target.

target.meaning: The required sum of the selected numbers.

box.meaning: A mapping from a previously seen number to its index.

num.meaning: The number at the current index.

needed.meaning: The complement required with num to reach target.

representation_requirements.description: Represent nums together with the current index and value.
Represent box as the mapping from seen values to their indices.
Represent the current scan state, including num and needed.
Represent lookup for needed before storing the current num.
Represent the selected pair of indices as the result.

semantic_invariants.statement: needed equals target minus num.
box contains indices only for values encountered before the current position.
A successful lookup uses a previously stored index and the current index.
The values at the returned indices sum to target.

completion_evidence.description: The learner identifies the complement relationship between num and target.
The learner traces how box changes during the scan.
The learner states or applies the lookup-before-store order.
The learner verifies that the returned indices satisfy the required sum.

terminal_behavior: Terminate and return the matching index pair when needed is found in box.
After scanning without a match, apply the problem's externally specified no-solution behavior.

problem.statement: Return true if any value appears at least twice in nums.

nums.meaning: The sequence of values to inspect.

box.meaning: The set of values encountered before the current num.

num.meaning: The value currently being inspected from nums.

representation_requirements.description: Represent nums in processing order and identify the current position.
Represent box as the distinct values encountered before the current num.
Represent checking whether num is in box before adding a new num.
Represent immediate true termination on a duplicate and false termination after exhaustion.

semantic_invariants.statement: A duplicate exists exactly when some value appears at least twice in nums.
Before processing the current num, box contains exactly the distinct values processed earlier in nums.
num is a duplicate exactly when num is already in box.
A non-duplicate num is added to box only after its membership has been checked.
The result is true if a duplicate is detected and false only after nums is exhausted without one.

completion_evidence.description: The learner identifies that any value appearing at least twice satisfies the condition.
The learner tracks how box represents previously processed values.
The learner states or applies the membership check before adding num.
The learner distinguishes duplicate-found termination from exhaustion without a duplicate.

terminal_behavior: Terminate and return true immediately when num is already in box.
Add num to box and continue when num is not already in box.
After all values are processed without a duplicate, return false.

problem.statement: Given prices, choose one buy day before one sell day to maximize profit.

prices.meaning: The sequence of prices ordered by day.

min_price.meaning: The lowest price among eligible earlier buy days.

price.meaning: The price at the current day being considered.

profit.meaning: The profit obtained by selling at price after buying at min_price.

best.meaning: The greatest eligible profit found so far.

representation_requirements.description: Represent prices in day order with the current price identified.
Represent min_price as the lowest price from earlier eligible buy days.
Represent the current profit and the maximum best value after each eligible sale day.
Represent best as the result after all eligible sale days have been evaluated.

semantic_invariants.statement: Every evaluated transaction uses a buy day strictly earlier than its sell day.
Before evaluating the current price as a sale, min_price equals the minimum price among earlier days.
profit equals price minus min_price for the current eligible sale day.
best equals the maximum profit among all eligible transactions evaluated so far.
Each price after the first is evaluated once as a sale candidate, and the current price becomes available for later buy days only afterward.

completion_evidence.description: The learner identifies that the buy day must precede the sell day.
The learner traces min_price as prices are scanned by day.
The learner computes profit and updates best while preserving their meanings.
The learner reconstructs the scan and identifies best after all eligible sale days are processed.

terminal_behavior: Evaluate every price after the first as a sale candidate using the minimum earlier price.
After evaluating the current sale candidate, incorporate the current price into min_price for later days.
After all eligible sale days are processed, return best.

problem.statement: Determine whether (), {}, [] brackets are correctly matched and nested.

s.meaning: The sequence of brackets to inspect.

stack.meaning: The unmatched opening brackets encountered while scanning s, with the most recent at the top.

ch.meaning: The bracket currently processed from s.

top.meaning: The most recent unmatched opening bracket in stack when stack is nonempty.

representation_requirements.description: Represent s in processing order and identify the current ch.
Represent stack as the ordered unmatched opening brackets, with the latest opening bracket at the top.
Represent whether a closing ch matches the current top opening bracket.
Represent immediate invalid termination on an unmatched or mismatched closing bracket and final validity based on an empty stack.

semantic_invariants.statement: A closing bracket must match the most recent unmatched opening bracket because nested brackets close in reverse opening order.
During the scan, stack contains exactly the opening brackets from the processed prefix that have not yet been matched.
A closing ch is valid only when stack is nonempty and top is its corresponding opening bracket; a successful match removes top.
The result is invalid if an unmatched or mismatched closing bracket is encountered, and is valid after exhaustion only when stack is empty.

completion_evidence.description: The learner identifies that matching depends on nested order and the most recent unmatched opening bracket.
The learner traces stack as the unmatched opening brackets in the processed prefix.
The learner applies the empty-stack and top-match checks before removing a matched opening bracket.
The learner distinguishes immediate invalid termination from valid completion with no unmatched opening brackets.

terminal_behavior: Scan s from left to right, processing each ch once.
Push each opening bracket onto stack.
For a closing bracket, return an invalid result immediately if stack is empty or top does not match ch; otherwise remove top.
After s is exhausted, return a valid result exactly when stack is empty.

problem.statement: Find target in sorted nums using binary search.

nums.meaning: A sequence sorted in nondecreasing order whose indices are searched.

target.meaning: The value whose position in nums is sought.

left.meaning: The smallest index currently eligible to contain target.

right.meaning: The largest index currently eligible to contain target.

mid.meaning: The index selected between left and right for the current comparison.

representation_requirements.description: Represent nums with indices and target to show how sorted order supports eliminating a side of the search space.
Show left and right as inclusive boundaries around the current candidate interval.
Show the current left and right values and the resulting midpoint index before comparison.
Contrast the boundary update when target is less than, greater than, or equal to nums[mid].
Represent the repeated compare-and-update procedure, including loop and terminal conditions.

semantic_invariants.statement: Because nums is sorted, comparing target with nums[mid] determines which side cannot contain target.
At every iteration, left and right delimit the inclusive candidate interval; any possible target index remains within that interval.
When left <= right, mid is an integer index satisfying left <= mid <= right and refers to nums[mid].
If nums[mid] < target, set left to mid + 1; if nums[mid] > target, set right to mid - 1; equality identifies mid as the found position.
Continue while left <= right; when left > right, no candidate index remains.

completion_evidence.description: States how sorted order makes one side of the search space safely discardable after comparison.
Identifies left and right as the inclusive bounds of the current candidate interval.
Determines the midpoint index from supplied left and right boundaries.
Selects the correct boundary update for each comparison outcome.
Reconstructs the compare, update, loop, found, and no-match termination behavior.

terminal_behavior: When nums[mid] equals target, terminate with mid as the found position.
When left exceeds right, terminate with a no-match outcome using the caller-specified convention.
If nums is empty, the initial interval is empty and the no-match behavior applies.

problem.statement: Reverse a singly linked list and return the new head.

prev.meaning: The first node of the already reversed prefix, or None when that prefix is empty.

curr.meaning: The node whose link is currently being reversed.

next_node.meaning: The node that originally followed curr and preserves the unreversed remainder before curr.next changes.

representation_requirements.description: Represent nodes in order with each next link and the current traversal position visible.
Represent prev, curr, and next_node before and after each iteration.
Represent next_node as the original successor of curr before rewiring curr.next.
Represent curr.next changing from its original successor to prev before the pointers advance.
Represent prev as the new head after curr becomes None.

semantic_invariants.statement: Each singly linked-list node has at most one outgoing next link that identifies its successor.
Before processing begins, prev is None and curr is the original head of the list.
Before curr.next is changed, next_node equals the original successor of curr and preserves access to the unreversed remainder.
After each iteration, the links from the original head through prev are reversed, curr is the first node of the unreversed remainder, and no unreversed node is lost.
When curr is None, prev is the head of the fully reversed list.

completion_evidence.description: The learner identifies the successor relationship represented by each next link.
The learner states the initial meanings and values of prev and curr.
The learner identifies next_node before changing curr.next.
The learner reconstructs the link reversal and pointer-advance sequence for an iteration.
The learner identifies the node held by prev when curr becomes None as the returned head.

terminal_behavior: Preserve curr's original successor in next_node before changing curr.next.
Set curr.next to prev, then advance prev to curr and curr to next_node.
When curr is None, return prev as the new head.

problem.statement: Merge two sorted linked lists into one sorted list.

a.meaning: The current node in the first sorted linked list.

b.meaning: The current node in the second sorted linked list.

tail.meaning: The last node currently linked in the merged sorted list.

head.meaning: The first node of the merged sorted list.

representation_requirements.description: Represent the current nodes referenced by a and b and their values when both lists remain nonempty.
Represent the merged sorted prefix and tail as nodes are linked in nondecreasing order.
Represent the unconsumed suffix of whichever input list remains after the other is exhausted.
Represent head as the entry point of the complete merged linked list.

semantic_invariants.statement: When both a and b are non-null, their values are the smallest unconsumed values in their respective lists.
The nodes from head through tail form a sorted merged prefix containing exactly the nodes consumed so far.
After one cursor becomes null, the other cursor references the complete remaining suffix that can be attached without further comparison.
When processing is complete, head references the first node of the merged list and the merged list contains every input node exactly once in sorted order.

completion_evidence.description: Identifies the current front nodes and compares their values while both lists remain.
Specifies selecting the smaller front node, linking it after tail, and advancing its source cursor.
Specifies attaching the non-null remaining cursor when one input list is exhausted.
Identifies head as the pointer to the complete merged sorted list.

terminal_behavior: Initialize the merged result with head and tail before repeatedly selecting nodes from the two list fronts.
While both a and b are non-null, link the smaller front node after tail, advance the selected cursor, and advance tail.
When either cursor is null, attach the non-null remaining cursor after tail.
Return head after all nodes from both input lists are included.

problem.statement: Return the maximum number of nodes from root down to a leaf.

node.meaning: The current binary-tree node being evaluated.

left_depth.meaning: The maximum number of nodes from node.left down to a leaf.

right_depth.meaning: The maximum number of nodes from node.right down to a leaf.

depth.meaning: The maximum number of nodes from node down to a leaf.

representation_requirements.description: Represent node and its left and right child references while evaluating the tree.
Represent an empty node as a subtree with depth zero.
Represent left_depth and right_depth as the completed depths of the two child subtrees.
Represent depth as one plus the greater of left_depth and right_depth for a non-empty node.

semantic_invariants.statement: depth counts nodes on the maximum path from the current node down to a leaf.
An empty subtree has depth 0.
left_depth and right_depth equal the maximum node counts of the left and right child subtrees.
For a non-empty node, depth equals 1 plus the maximum of left_depth and right_depth.

completion_evidence.description: Identifies the result as the maximum root-to-leaf node count.
Specifies depth 0 for an empty subtree.
Obtains both child depths before computing the current node's depth.
Computes the current depth as 1 plus the larger child depth.

terminal_behavior: At an empty node, return 0.
At a non-empty node, compute left_depth and right_depth from the child subtrees.
Set depth to 1 plus the greater of left_depth and right_depth.
Return depth for the root node.

problem.statement: Find shortest number of edges from start to goal in an unweighted graph.

queue.meaning: A FIFO collection of discovered nodes awaiting processing.

node.meaning: The node currently removed from queue for processing.

dist.meaning: A mapping from each discovered node to its number of edges from start.

neighbors.meaning: The nodes directly connected to node by an edge.

representation_requirements.description: Represent the unweighted graph so each node's neighbors can be inspected, with start and goal identifiable.
Show queue as a FIFO frontier and dist as the recorded edge distance for discovered nodes.
Trace dequeue and enqueue operations in FIFO order to make breadth-by-distance processing explicit.
Show each unvisited neighbor when it is first assigned a distance and added to queue.
Represent the goal distance when reached and an explicit unreachable result when the frontier is exhausted.

semantic_invariants.statement: Each traversed graph edge contributes exactly one to path length.
The start node has distance 0, and each discovered node has a recorded number of edges from start.
FIFO processing removes nodes in nondecreasing order of their recorded distance.
When a node is first discovered, its assigned distance is the shortest distance from start in the unweighted graph.
If the goal is reached, its recorded distance is the shortest number of edges; if the queue is exhausted first, the goal is unreachable.

completion_evidence.description: The graph representation identifies nodes, the start, the goal, and each node's neighbor relation.
The algorithm state shows start in queue with distance 0 and a consistent representation for undiscovered nodes.
A trace shows FIFO expansion, first-time neighbor discovery, and distance assignment one edge beyond the current node.
The result identifies the shortest edge count for a reached goal or an explicit unreachable outcome after frontier exhaustion.

terminal_behavior: If start equals goal, the shortest number of edges is 0.
If the goal is reached, return its recorded distance.
If the queue is exhausted before the goal is reached, return an explicit unreachable result.

problem.statement: Count connected groups of 1s in a 2D grid using 4-direction adjacency.

grid.meaning: The input 2D grid whose 1 cells represent land and whose 0 cells represent non-land or already marked cells.

r.meaning: The current row index being scanned or explored.

c.meaning: The current column index being scanned or explored.

count.meaning: The number of connected land components whose exploration has been initiated.

stack.meaning: The collection of discovered land-cell coordinates awaiting neighbor expansion.

representation_requirements.description: Represent grid coordinates in a deterministic row-and-column scan with the current cell identified.
Represent only the side-sharing neighbors above, below, left, and right of the current cell.
Represent an unmarked 1 cell as the seed that starts one component exploration.
Represent discovered land cells as marked in grid so they cannot start or join another exploration.
Represent discovered but not yet expanded land-cell coordinates in stack.
Represent count increasing once for each newly discovered component seed.
Represent count after every grid cell has been scanned and every discovered component has been fully expanded.

semantic_invariants.statement: An adjacent cell is eligible only when it shares a side with the current cell: (r-1,c), (r+1,c), (r,c-1), or (r,c+1).
count increases exactly when the scan encounters a grid cell whose current value is 1 and which has not already been marked.
A land cell is changed from 1 to 0 when it is added to stack, so it cannot be added again.
Every coordinate in stack belongs to the same connected component as the seed currently being explored.
count equals the number of distinct connected components whose seeds have been encountered and whose flood-fill explorations have been initiated.
After the scan completes, every original 1 cell has been marked 0 and belongs to exactly one counted component.

completion_evidence.description: Identifies side-sharing neighbors and excludes diagonal adjacency.
Tracks the grid scan and identifies when an unmarked 1 cell starts a new component.
Tracks stack and grid as one component is expanded through eligible neighbors.
Preserves the order of marking a discovered land cell before adding it to stack.
Distinguishes starting a component from expanding cells already belonging to it.
Verifies count after all rows and columns have been processed.

terminal_behavior: Scan every row and column in deterministic order.
When grid[r][c] is 1, increment count, mark the seed cell as 0, and add its coordinate to stack.
While stack is nonempty, expand each coordinate through its four in-bounds side-sharing neighbors; mark and add each neighbor whose current value is 1.
After stack becomes empty, continue the grid scan for another unmarked 1 cell.
After all grid cells are scanned, return count.

problem.statement: Find the kth largest value using a min-heap of size k.

nums.meaning: The sequence of values to process.

k.meaning: The requested largest-value rank and maximum heap size.

heap.meaning: A min-heap containing the largest values retained from the processed prefix.

num.meaning: The value currently being processed from nums.

representation_requirements.description: Represent nums in processing order and identify the current num.
Represent heap as a min-heap whose root is its minimum value.
Represent the size of heap relative to k during processing.
Represent inserting num before removing the minimum when heap exceeds size k.
Represent the minimum element of heap as the final kth-largest value.

semantic_invariants.statement: Among k retained values, the minimum value is the kth largest of those values.
After initialization and each completed update, heap contains no more than k values.
Immediately after inserting num, heap contains the prior retained values plus num before size correction.
After size correction for each processed prefix, heap contains the k largest values in that prefix when the prefix has at least k values, and otherwise contains all prefix values.
After all nums are processed with valid 1 <= k <= len(nums), the minimum element of heap is the kth largest value.

completion_evidence.description: The response connects the kth-largest rank to the minimum of the retained top-k values.
The response represents heap initialization and its size bound relative to k.
The response states or applies insertion of each current num before size correction.
The response traces removal of the minimum whenever heap exceeds size k and preserves the top-k invariant.
The response identifies the minimum element of the final heap as the requested value.

terminal_behavior: Process each num in nums by inserting it into heap.
Whenever heap contains more than k values, remove its minimum value before continuing.
After nums is exhausted, return the minimum element of heap as the kth largest value for valid 1 <= k <= len(nums).

problem.statement: Find the maximum sum of any contiguous window of size k.

p.meaning: The one-based position of a value in a.

i.meaning: The zero-based starting index of the current window.

k.meaning: The number of consecutive values included in each window.

box.meaning: The current group of exactly k consecutive values starting at index i.

S.meaning: The sequence of sums for valid windows, indexed by their starting index.

j.meaning: The offset k - 1 used to identify the rightmost position of the current window.

max_sum.meaning: The largest valid window sum found so far.

representation_requirements.description: Represent a with its values and their one-based positions p.
Represent box as exactly k adjacent values in a.
Represent the relationship i = p - 1 for the current value.
Represent S[i] as the sum of the k values in the window beginning at i.
Represent one-position movement of the window, including the outgoing left value and incoming right value.
Represent each new sum using the previous sum, the outgoing value a[i-1], and the incoming value a[i+j].
Represent max_sum as the greatest S[i] encountered so far.
Represent processing of every starting index that produces a complete size-k window.
Represent max_sum after all valid windows have been considered.

semantic_invariants.statement: Every considered window consists of consecutive elements of a with no gaps.
Every considered window contains exactly k values.
For the same value, the zero-based index i equals its one-based position p minus 1.
S[i] equals the sum of the k values from a[i] through a[i+k-1] when the window begins at i.
Moving from one valid start index to the next removes a[i-1] and adds a[i+j], where j equals k-1.
For each later valid window, S[i] equals S[i-1] - a[i-1] + a[i+j].
max_sum equals the largest window sum among the valid windows processed so far.
Only complete size-k windows are processed, and every valid starting index is considered before returning max_sum.

completion_evidence.description: The learner identifies the values and boundaries of a contiguous group containing exactly k elements.
The learner translates between one-based position p and zero-based index i consistently.
The learner determines S[i] from the k values in the initial window.
The learner identifies the outgoing and incoming values and preserves the rolling-sum update order.
The learner maintains max_sum as the greatest processed window sum.
The learner verifies that all complete windows were processed and that max_sum is the returned result.

terminal_behavior: Consider only windows containing exactly k consecutive values.
Initialize the first valid window sum directly from its k values.
For each later valid start index i, update S[i] by removing a[i-1] and adding a[i+j], with j = k - 1.
Update max_sum whenever the current window sum is larger than the stored maximum.
After all valid windows are processed, return max_sum.

intervals.meaning: the input intervals ordered by nondecreasing start for the scan

current.meaning: the interval representing the current overlapping group

next_interval.meaning: the next interval considered after current

merged.meaning: finalized non-overlapping intervals emitted before the active current interval

representation_requirements.description: Represent the intervals in scan order with their endpoints visible.
Show current and next_interval on a number line for an overlap decision.
Track current, next_interval, and merged across each scan step.
Trace finalization of current and the resulting merged collection.

semantic_invariants.statement: The scan processes intervals in nondecreasing start order, so current precedes next_interval.
current and next_interval overlap when next_interval begins at or before current ends; otherwise next_interval begins after current ends.
current spans every interval in the active group, while merged contains only groups already closed and remains ordered without overlap.
After finalization, merged represents every input interval exactly once as a sorted, non-overlapping interval partition.

completion_evidence.description: Learner explains why establishing interval order supports a forward scan.
Learner predicts whether current and next_interval overlap from their endpoint positions.
Learner reconstructs whether to extend current or commit it to merged.
Learner reconstructs finalization of current and describes the completed merged collection.

terminal_behavior: After all intervals are scanned, append the remaining current interval to merged exactly once.
Treat merged as the final collection of sorted, non-overlapping intervals.

problem.statement: Check whether a string is a palindrome while ignoring non-alphanumeric characters and case.

s.meaning: The input string whose characters are inspected from both ends.

left.meaning: The index of the current character considered from the left side of s.

right.meaning: The index of the current character considered from the right side of s.

representation_requirements.description: Represent s in index order with character positions visible.
Represent the alphanumeric characters of s in their original order while excluding non-alphanumeric characters from comparison.
Represent left and right as positions that move inward to the next relevant characters.
Represent endpoint characters in a case-insensitive form before deciding whether they match.
Represent false on a relevant-character mismatch and true after all relevant endpoint pairs agree.

semantic_invariants.statement: The string satisfies the required condition exactly when corresponding relevant characters from opposite ends match without regard to case.
Before an endpoint comparison, left and right identify alphanumeric characters or have crossed after skipping non-alphanumeric characters.
An endpoint pair matches exactly when the characters at left and right are equal after case normalization.
After a matching endpoint comparison, left advances inward and right retreats inward, so the unprocessed region strictly shrinks.
A mismatch between any pair of relevant endpoint characters determines a false result immediately.
If the pointers cross or meet without a mismatch, every relevant endpoint pair has matched and the result is true.

completion_evidence.description: The learner identifies that the condition compares corresponding relevant characters from opposite ends.
The learner traces left and right while skipping non-alphanumeric characters.
The learner applies case-insensitive endpoint comparison and moves both pointers inward after a match.
The learner distinguishes immediate false termination on mismatch from true termination after the pointers meet or cross.

terminal_behavior: Skip non-alphanumeric characters before comparing the characters at left and right.
Return false immediately when the normalized characters at left and right differ.
After matching endpoints, move left inward and right inward until the pointers meet or cross.
Return true when the pointers meet or cross without a mismatch.
